domain_entities.name: Employee
domain_entities.purpose: The authenticated caller and the subject of leave/balance reads. Gains a nullable passwordHash credential so a caller can authenticate; null means the employee has no login credential yet.

domain_entities.name: AuthToken
domain_entities.purpose: A bearer credential minted on successful login. Its payload contract is fixed by the existing verifier: sub = employee id, role = EmployeeRole. Stateless; validity is derived from expiry, not stored.

domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: The read subject of GET /leaves and GET /leaves/:id. No new fields or states; this feature only defines who may read it (role-scoped visibility).

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: The read subject of GET /balances/me. The current balance is the row whose accrual period contains today; the period is derived from the employee's hireDate (same derivation as LeaveService.resolveBalance).

business_rules: Login failure is indistinguishable: a wrong email and a wrong password produce the same status and the same message, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate accounts. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Authentication appears, not only here]

The password_hash credential must never appear in any response body; only the caller's own profile (and never the hash) is returned on login. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Employee credential appears, not only here]

The token payload contract is fixed: sub = employee id, role = EmployeeRole. No other claims are added; the existing verifier is the consumer and its contract is not changed. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever AuthToken appears, not only here]

Leave visibility is role-scoped: EMPLOYEE sees only their own requests; MANAGER sees their own plus those of employees whose managerId is the manager; ADMIN sees all. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest visibility appears, not only here]

A caller who may not see a leave request receives the same response as one that does not exist (same status, same message), so the endpoint cannot be used to probe for ids. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest visibility appears, not only here]
The actor for every read is resolved from the authenticated token (request.user), never from a client-supplied id. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Actor resolution appears, not only here]

The current leave balance is the row whose accrual period contains today; the accrual period is derived from the employee's hireDate exactly as LeaveService.resolveBalance does it (reused, not re-derived). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance accrual period appears, not only here]
Read endpoints must not write and must not open a transaction. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever Read operations appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
Authentication and read endpoints add no new lifecycle states to existing entities. Employee gains a nullable `passwordHash` credential (no new state — ACTIVE/TERMINATED/ON_LEAVE unchanged). A new value object `AuthToken` is introduced with lifecycle ISSUED → EXPIRED (expiry derived from the signed `expiresIn`, not stored). LeaveRequest and LeaveBalance are read-only subjects here: their existing lifecycle states (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED; OPEN/CLOSED) are unchanged and no transitions are added.

Binding business rules (scope broad): (1) login failure is indistinguishable between wrong email and wrong password; (2) password_hash never appears in any response; (3) token payload contract is fixed as sub=employee id, role=EmployeeRole (the existing verifier is the consumer); (4) leave visibility is role-scoped (EMPLOYEE=own, MANAGER=own+direct reports via managerId, ADMIN=all); (5) a caller who may not see a request gets the same response as a nonexistent id; (6) actor is always resolved from request.user, never a client-supplied id; (7) the current balance's accrual period is derived from hireDate exactly as LeaveService.resolveBalance does (reused, not re-derived); (8) read endpoints never write and never open a transaction.

Open questions for the chief: (a) date-range filter edge inclusivity for GET /leaves (must match existing findByQuery semantics); (b) whether GET /balances/me returns one leave type or all types, since balances are per leave type.

open_questions.question: Are the date-range filter boundaries (startDateFrom/startDateTo/endDateFrom/endDateTo) inclusive or exclusive at each edge?
open_questions.impact: Affects which leave requests are returned by GET /leaves for a given filter; a wrong choice silently drops or includes boundary-day requests. Must be consistent with the existing LeaveRepository.findByQuery semantics.
candidate_options: Inclusive on both edges (startDate >= from AND startDate <= to)
Inclusive lower bound, exclusive upper bound
Match the existing findByQuery SQL semantics exactly

open_questions.question: GET /balances/me returns "the caller's current leave balance" — but balances are per leave type. Which leave type (or all types) is returned?
open_questions.impact: Determines the response shape (single balance vs list) and whether the endpoint must filter by leaveTypeCode. The feature text says "the caller's current leave balance" (singular) but the domain has one balance per leave type.
candidate_options: Return all leave-type balances for the current period
Return a single balance keyed by a required leaveTypeCode query param
